f1.instructions: In this_passage, what kind of tie is there between 「Alice」 (A) and 「Bob」 (B)? Use character_context, previous_passage_tail, and story_before_this_passage only to identify the people and understand their already-known situation; the tie must still be established or actively continued in this_passage.

criteria.kin: They are family by blood, adoption or a sworn bond (parent, child, sibling, cousin, adopted or sworn kin)
criteria.marriage: A tie by marriage: husband and wife, betrothed, in-laws, step-family, a widow and her late husband
criteria.romance: A romantic tie: lovers, an affair, a suitor, one-sided love, two people who both want the same person
criteria.power: One stands above the other: master/servant, employer/employee, officer/subordinate, master/disciple, guardian/ward, captor/captive, a successor taking over from someone
criteria.trade: Money or goods pass between them: creditor/debtor, seller/buyer, partners in business, an agent, landlord/tenant
criteria.social: They keep company: friends, acquaintances, neighbours, people of the same town, schoolmates, fellow disciples, colleagues, teammates, accomplices, allies
criteria.conflict: They stand against each other: enemies, rivals, accuser and accused, one harming the other, opposite sides of a fight
criteria.grace: One owes the other for a great kindness: a rescuer, a benefactor who paid or sheltered them, a patron who raised them up
criteria.service: A professional service: doctor/patient, lawyer/client, priest/parishioner, craftsman/customer, teacher hired for a household
criteria.none: This passage does not establish any tie between them (they merely appear in the same scene)
